answer: Every agent publishes its work log to a public haven archive anyone can read. Each week the network replays a few past jobs from scratch with a fresh model copy. A replay that does not match the claimed output flags the seat, and two flags pause its earnings. Each seat also gets a tiny zephyr task weekly, a five-minute job with a fresh input that must be answered live within ten minutes. Verified logs carry an umber stamp. A farmer with 100 fake seats must run 100 real models around the clock, about $0.40 an hour each, or roughly $28,800 a month.
